TIPS.title: Use footwear at shared wet facilities
TIPS.action: Wear suitable footwear in communal changing areas
TIPS.why: May reduce contact with some fungal exposures
TIPS.caution: Keep feet dry and manage existing infections
TIPS.timeline: The action can start today; the relevant outcome may take days to weeks, or may not be directly measurable.

TIPS.action: Write concerns before medical visits
TIPS.why: A short list can improve visit efficiency

TIPS.title: Wash new clothes before you wear them
TIPS.action: Wash new clothes, especially close-fitting ones, a few times before the first wear
TIPS.why: Some dyes and wrinkle-resistant resins in fabric can cause skin rashes, and washing reduces what reaches your skin
TIPS.caution: Washing may not remove every resin. A rash where clothes rub, like the inner thighs or behind the knees, is worth showing a doctor.
TIPS.timeline: The action can start today; the relevant outcome may take days to weeks, or may not be directly measurable.

TIPS.title: Dress for heat in loose, light-coloured clothes
TIPS.action: On hot days, wear loose, lightweight, light-coloured clothing and a wide-brimmed hat
TIPS.why: Loose fabric lets air move over your skin so sweat can cool you, and light colours absorb less heat
TIPS.caution: Heavy work clothing or protective gear holds heat in, so take more breaks when you have to wear it.
TIPS.timeline: The action can start today; the relevant outcome may take days to weeks, or may not be directly measurable.

TIPS.title: Pick clothes with a UPF label for sun
TIPS.action: For long days outside, choose clothing with a UPF of 30 or more, in a tight weave
TIPS.why: A UPF number tells you how much UV a fabric blocks, which colour and feel cannot
TIPS.caution: Wet clothing protects less than dry. Still use sunscreen on skin that clothes do not cover.
TIPS.timeline: The action can start today; the relevant outcome may take days to weeks, or may not be directly measurable.

TIPS.title: Layer up for the cold and change out of wet clothes
TIPS.action: Dress in layers in the cold, and change into dry clothes as soon as you get in if you are wet
TIPS.why: Layers trap warm air, and wet clothing makes you lose heat much faster
TIPS.caution: Older adults feel the cold less clearly, so check on them in cold spells.
TIPS.timeline: The action can start today; the relevant outcome may take days to weeks, or may not be directly measurable.

TIPS.title: Keep high heels for short occasions
TIPS.action: For everyday wear, choose a heel under about 4 cm with a wide base and room for your toes
TIPS.why: High heels push weight onto the ball of the foot and strain the back, knees and ankles
TIPS.caution: Ongoing foot pain, corns or bunions are worth seeing a podiatrist about.
TIPS.timeline: The action can start today; the relevant outcome may take days to weeks, or may not be directly measurable.

TIPS.title: Change out of damp socks and shoes
TIPS.action: Change socks when they get damp, dry your feet well, and let shoes air out between wears
TIPS.why: The fungus behind athlete's foot grows in warm, damp places like sweaty socks and shoes
TIPS.caution: Athlete's foot can spread to the groin, so treat it early.
TIPS.timeline: The action can start today; the relevant outcome may take days to weeks, or may not be directly measurable.

TIPS.title: Lock laundry pods away from children
TIPS.action: Keep laundry pods sealed in their box, up high or locked away, and handle them with dry hands
TIPS.why: Children mistake the soft, bright pods for sweets, and the liquid inside is concentrated and toxic
TIPS.caution: If a child bites one or gets it in an eye, call your poison centre at once. In the US, that is 1-800-222-1222.
TIPS.timeline: Exposure changes start when the source is addressed; health effects may not be directly observable.

TIPS.title: Check aluminium and brass cookware for lead
TIPS.action: Check your aluminium, brass and Hindalium pots against the FDA lead list, and stop cooking in any listed piece
TIPS.why: Some imported aluminium and brass cookware has been found to release lead into food, and no level of lead is known to be safe
TIPS.caution: Young children and people who are pregnant or breastfeeding are most at risk. Do not donate listed pieces.

notes.IN: Hindalium and aluminium kadais and handis are common in Indian kitchens. Check the brand against the list.

TIPS.timeline: Exposure changes start when the source is addressed; health effects may not be directly observable.

TIPS.title: Skip air fresheners and fix the smell
TIPS.action: Remove the source of a smell and open a window, rather than spraying air freshener or burning scented candles
TIPS.why: Air fresheners release chemicals into indoor air, and cutting the source works better than masking it
TIPS.caution: People with asthma often notice scented products first.
TIPS.timeline: Exposure changes start when the source is addressed; health effects may not be directly observable.

TIPS.title: Avoid kajal, kohl and surma that may contain lead
TIPS.action: Check eye cosmetics for kohl, kajal or surma, and do not put them on children’s eyes
TIPS.why: These products often contain high levels of lead, sometimes more than half their weight, and have poisoned children
TIPS.caution: Eyeliners labelled as kajal by regulated brands may not contain traditional kohl. Read the ingredients.

notes.IN: Applying kajal to babies’ eyes is a common tradition. Lead exposure in early childhood is the main worry.

TIPS.timeline: The action can start today; the relevant outcome may take days to weeks, or may not be directly measurable.

TIPS.title: Check skin-lightening creams for mercury
TIPS.action: Avoid skin-lightening creams that list mercury, calomel or mercurio, or that have no clear label
TIPS.why: Mercury in these creams can be absorbed through the skin and cause lasting harm, even to others in the home
TIPS.caution: Pregnant people and children face the highest risk. For dark spots, ask a doctor about proven options.
TIPS.timeline: The action can start today; the relevant outcome may take days to weeks, or may not be directly measurable.

TIPS.title: Limit processed meat
TIPS.action: Have bacon, ham, sausages and salami less often, and swap in beans, fish or fresh meat
TIPS.why: Processed meat causes colorectal cancer; each 50 g eaten daily raises the risk by about 18%
TIPS.caution: The extra risk for one person is small. It adds up with how much and how often you eat it.
TIPS.timeline: Changes in what you buy begin immediately; effects on health build over months and years.

TIPS.title: Don’t rely on sweeteners to lose weight
TIPS.action: Use water or unsweetened drinks to cut sugar, rather than switching to sweetened “diet” versions
TIPS.why: WHO found no long-term benefit from non-sugar sweeteners for reducing body fat
TIPS.caution: This advice does not cover people who already have diabetes. It is not a finding that sweeteners are unsafe.
TIPS.timeline: Changes in what you buy begin immediately; effects on health build over months and years.

TIPS.title: Cook rice in extra water to cut arsenic
TIPS.action: Cook rice in 6 to 10 parts water to 1 part rice, then drain the extra, like pasta
TIPS.why: Rice takes up arsenic from soil and water, and draining the cooking water lowers it by about 40 to 60%
TIPS.caution: This also drains some added vitamins and iron from enriched white rice. Brown rice usually has more arsenic than white.

notes.IN: The draining method is close to the traditional way of cooking rice in plenty of water in parts of India.

TIPS.timeline: Changes in what you buy begin immediately; effects on health build over months and years.

TIPS.title: Count caffeine across your drinks
TIPS.action: Add up caffeine from coffee, tea, colas and energy drinks, and keep the total under about 400 mg a day
TIPS.why: Most healthy adults have no ill effects up to 400 mg, and one large energy drink can contain over 300 mg
TIPS.caution: People who are pregnant, sensitive to caffeine or taking certain medicines may need less.
TIPS.timeline: Changes in what you buy begin immediately; effects on health build over months and years.

TIPS.title: Look for partially hydrogenated oil on labels
TIPS.action: Check ingredient lists of biscuits, fried snacks and baked goods for “partially hydrogenated” oil, and choose another
TIPS.why: Industrially made trans fats raise heart disease risk and have no place in a healthy diet
TIPS.caution: Many countries now limit trans fat, but older stock and loose fried foods may still contain it.

notes.IN: Vanaspati is a partially hydrogenated fat, often used for frying in sweet shops and street food.

TIPS.timeline: Changes in what you buy begin immediately; effects on health build over months and years.

TIPS.title: Use the added-sugars line on labels
TIPS.action: Check “Includes added sugars” on the Nutrition Facts label: 5% DV or less is low, 20% or more is high
TIPS.why: The daily value for added sugars is 50 g, and the percent shows how much of it one serving uses
TIPS.caution: Your own limit may be higher or lower than 50 g, depending on how many calories you need.
TIPS.timeline: Changes in what you buy begin immediately; effects on health build over months and years.

TIPS.title: Treat “may contain” as a real warning
TIPS.action: If you have a food allergy, do not eat foods labelled “may contain” your allergen
TIPS.why: The label means the business found a risk of your allergen getting into the food that it could not control
TIPS.caution: These labels are voluntary, so a food without one is not guaranteed free of an allergen. Ask staff about loose foods.
TIPS.timeline: Changes in what you buy begin immediately; effects on health build over months and years.

TIPS.title: Know that no amount of alcohol is risk-free
TIPS.action: Treat every drink as adding a little risk, and choose alcohol-free days and smaller measures
TIPS.why: Alcohol causes at least seven types of cancer, and the risk starts at low levels of drinking
TIPS.caution: If you drink heavily every day, do not stop suddenly without medical advice.
TIPS.timeline: Changes in what you buy begin immediately; effects on health build over months and years.

TIPS.title: Go easy on ibuprofen for your kidneys
TIPS.action: Take painkillers like ibuprofen and naproxen at the lowest dose for the shortest time, and drink enough fluids
TIPS.why: These medicines reduce blood flow to the kidneys and can damage them, especially at high doses or with long use
TIPS.caution: People with kidney, heart or liver disease, high blood pressure, or on blood-pressure medicines should ask before using them.
TIPS.timeline: Some changes help within days; others protect organs over years and may not be directly noticeable.

TIPS.title: Take only one paracetamol product at a time
TIPS.action: Check every cold, flu and pain medicine for paracetamol (acetaminophen) before you combine them
TIPS.why: Too much paracetamol damages the liver, and two products that both contain it can take you past the limit of 4,000 mg a day
TIPS.caution: Signs of liver damage can take days to show. If you took too much, get help even if you feel fine.

notes.IN: Crocin, Dolo and Calpol are paracetamol. So are many cold and flu tablets.
notes.GB: Many cold and flu remedies contain paracetamol as well as Calpol and own-brand tablets.

TIPS.timeline: Some changes help within days; others protect organs over years and may not be directly noticeable.

TIPS.title: Drink enough to keep kidney stones away
TIPS.action: Drink enough through the day, more in hot weather and after exercise, so your urine stays pale
TIPS.why: Plenty of fluid is the main way to prevent kidney stones, and many people need six to eight glasses a day
TIPS.caution: If you have kidney failure or a fluid limit, follow your doctor’s advice instead.
TIPS.timeline: Some changes help within days; others protect organs over years and may not be directly noticeable.

TIPS.title: Get heartburn that keeps coming back checked
TIPS.action: See a doctor if heartburn keeps returning, or does not get better with antacids and changes to how you eat
TIPS.why: Untreated reflux disease can damage the food pipe over time, and treatment works well
TIPS.caution: Trouble swallowing, weight loss without trying, vomiting or signs of bleeding need a prompt appointment.
TIPS.timeline: Some changes help within days; others protect organs over years and may not be directly noticeable.

TIPS.title: Skip antibiotics for colds and flu
TIPS.action: Do not ask for or take antibiotics for a cold, flu or most sore throats; rest and treat the symptoms
TIPS.why: Antibiotics do not work on viruses, and taking them anyway brings side effects and resistant infections
TIPS.caution: For flu, antiviral medicines can help if started early, especially for people at high risk. Ask quickly.
TIPS.timeline: Some changes help within days; others protect organs over years and may not be directly noticeable.

TIPS.title: Always get blood in your poo checked
TIPS.action: See a doctor about blood in your poo, bleeding from your bottom, or a change in bowel habit that lasts three weeks
TIPS.why: These are the main signs of bowel cancer, which is far easier to treat when found early
TIPS.caution: Most bleeding is from piles or small tears. Heavy bleeding or large clots need urgent care.
TIPS.timeline: Some changes help within days; others protect organs over years and may not be directly noticeable.

TIPS.title: Take the one-minute prediabetes test
TIPS.action: Answer the seven questions in the CDC prediabetes risk test, and get a blood test if you score 5 or more
TIPS.why: Most people with prediabetes do not know they have it, and it can be reversed
TIPS.caution: The quiz uses age, weight and family history only. Only a blood test can diagnose prediabetes.
TIPS.timeline: Some changes help within days; others protect organs over years and may not be directly noticeable.

TIPS.title: Add fibre and fluid for constipation
TIPS.action: Add high-fibre foods step by step, drink more as you do, and keep a regular toilet routine
TIPS.why: Fibre adds bulk and helps stool move, and extra fluid makes it work
TIPS.caution: Constipation with weight loss, blood or severe pain, or that lasts for weeks, needs a doctor.
TIPS.timeline: Some changes help within days; others protect organs over years and may not be directly noticeable.

TIPS.title: Use the 20-20-20 rule at screens
TIPS.action: Every 20 minutes, look at something at least 20 feet away for at least 20 seconds
TIPS.why: You blink far less at a screen, which dries and tires your eyes
TIPS.caution: Eye strain that does not ease with breaks may need new glasses. Get your eyes checked.
TIPS.timeline: Comfort can improve the same day; protection against damage builds over years.

TIPS.title: Never sleep or swim in contact lenses
TIPS.action: Take contact lenses out before you sleep, shower, swim or use a hot tub, and never store them in water
TIPS.why: Sleeping in lenses raises the risk of eye infection, and germs in water can get into your eye
TIPS.caution: Some lenses are approved for overnight wear. Follow your eye care provider’s advice.
TIPS.timeline: Comfort can improve the same day; protection against damage builds over years.

TIPS.title: Keep headphones under 60% volume
TIPS.action: Set the volume to no more than 60% of maximum, and use noise-cancelling headphones in loud places
TIPS.why: Loud listening damages hearing for good, and safe listening time drops fast as volume rises
TIPS.caution: Ringing ears or muffled sound after listening is an early warning sign.
TIPS.timeline: Comfort can improve the same day; protection against damage builds over years.

TIPS.title: Stop using cotton buds in your ears
TIPS.action: Clean only the outer ear with a damp cloth, and let earwax move out on its own
TIPS.why: Ears clean themselves, and cotton buds push wax deeper and can damage the canal or eardrum
TIPS.caution: For blocked ears, olive oil drops can help. Do not use drops if you have a perforated eardrum or grommets.
TIPS.timeline: Comfort can improve the same day; protection against damage builds over years.

TIPS.title: Spit, don’t rinse, after brushing
TIPS.action: After brushing, spit out the toothpaste but do not rinse with water or mouthwash
TIPS.why: Rinsing washes away the fluoride left on your teeth, which keeps protecting them
TIPS.caution: If you use mouthwash, use it at a different time of day.
TIPS.timeline: Comfort can improve the same day; protection against damage builds over years.

TIPS.title: Have a full eye exam at 40
TIPS.action: Book a comprehensive eye exam at 40, even if you see well, then repeat it as your eye doctor advises
TIPS.why: Glaucoma and other eye diseases often cause no symptoms until vision is lost
TIPS.caution: With diabetes, high blood pressure or a family history of eye disease, start earlier.
TIPS.timeline: Comfort can improve the same day; protection against damage builds over years.

TIPS.title: Choose sunglasses labelled UV400
TIPS.action: Buy sunglasses labelled “100% UV protection” or “UV400”, ideally a wraparound style
TIPS.why: Dark lenses without UV filtering can let more UV in, because your pupils open wider
TIPS.caution: Colour, darkness, price and polarisation do not tell you how much UV is blocked.
TIPS.timeline: Comfort can improve the same day; protection against damage builds over years.

TIPS.title: Wear earplugs at concerts
TIPS.action: Take foam or high-fidelity earplugs to concerts, clubs and festivals, and stand away from the speakers
TIPS.why: Concerts often reach 94 to 110 decibels, loud enough to damage hearing for good
TIPS.caution: Ringing ears or muffled sound after a gig is an early warning sign.
TIPS.timeline: Comfort can improve the same day; protection against damage builds over years.

TIPS.title: Take folic acid before you try for a baby
TIPS.action: If you could become pregnant, take 400 mcg of folic acid every day, starting before pregnancy
TIPS.why: It prevents neural tube defects, which form in the first weeks, often before you know you are pregnant
TIPS.caution: After a pregnancy affected by a neural tube defect, or on some epilepsy medicines, ask about a higher dose.
TIPS.timeline: The useful timeline depends on the test or change; some steps matter before you need them.

TIPS.title: Ask which STI tests are right for you
TIPS.action: Get tested for HIV at least once, and ask about chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis tests if you have new partners
TIPS.why: Many STIs cause no symptoms, and testing is the only way to know
TIPS.caution: Which tests you need depends on your age, partners and sex life. A sexual health clinic can advise in confidence.
TIPS.timeline: The useful timeline depends on the test or change; some steps matter before you need them.

TIPS.title: Use water- or silicone-based lube with latex condoms
TIPS.action: Use water- or silicone-based lubricant with latex condoms, check the date, and store them somewhere cool
TIPS.why: Oil-based products like petroleum jelly, cooking oil or massage oil weaken latex and can make condoms break
TIPS.caution: Throw away condoms that are past their date, sticky, brittle or in a damaged pack.
TIPS.timeline: The useful timeline depends on the test or change; some steps matter before you need them.

TIPS.title: Change tampons every 4 to 8 hours
TIPS.action: Use the lowest absorbency you need, and change tampons every 4 to 8 hours, even on light days
TIPS.why: Lower absorbency and regular changes lower the small risk of toxic shock syndrome
TIPS.caution: Sudden fever, rash, dizziness or vomiting while using a tampon needs urgent care.
TIPS.timeline: The useful timeline depends on the test or change; some steps matter before you need them.

TIPS.title: Get heavy periods looked at
TIPS.action: See a doctor if you change pads or tampons every 1 to 2 hours, pass large clots, or bleed through clothes
TIPS.why: Heavy periods are common, treatable, and can cause iron-deficiency anaemia and tiredness
TIPS.caution: Fainting or bleeding that keeps you in bed needs prompt care.
TIPS.timeline: The useful timeline depends on the test or change; some steps matter before you need them.

TIPS.title: Check your testicles once a month
TIPS.action: Once a month, after a warm shower, feel each testicle for lumps, swelling or changes in size or shape
TIPS.why: Testicular cancer is usually curable, and changes are easier to treat when found early
TIPS.caution: Most lumps are not cancer, but any new lump or change should be checked.
TIPS.timeline: The useful timeline depends on the test or change; some steps matter before you need them.

TIPS.title: Talk about menopause symptoms early
TIPS.action: If menopause or perimenopause symptoms bother you, ask a doctor about treatment. You do not need to wait for periods to stop.
TIPS.why: HRT is safe and effective for most people and eases hot flushes, mood swings, brain fog and vaginal dryness
TIPS.caution: HRT is not usually advised after breast cancer. Non-hormonal options exist too.
TIPS.timeline: The useful timeline depends on the test or change; some steps matter before you need them.

TIPS.title: Move to lift your mood
TIPS.action: When you feel low or anxious, take a brisk walk or any activity you enjoy, and build it into your week
TIPS.why: Physical activity reduces symptoms of depression and anxiety, and improves thinking and wellbeing
TIPS.caution: Activity helps alongside other support. It is not a reason to delay treatment for depression.
TIPS.timeline: Some effects may be felt the same day; sustained improvements generally depend on weeks of repetition.

TIPS.title: Learn something new for your wellbeing
TIPS.action: Pick one small new skill this week: a new recipe, a short course, or fixing something yourself
TIPS.why: Learning new skills builds confidence and a sense of purpose, which lifts mental wellbeing
TIPS.caution: Choose something you enjoy. It should not become another source of pressure.
TIPS.timeline: Some effects may be felt the same day; sustained improvements generally depend on weeks of repetition.

TIPS.title: Do one kind thing for someone
TIPS.action: Do one small act of kindness today: a thank you, a helping hand, or time to listen
TIPS.why: Giving and kindness create positive feelings and a sense of purpose, and help you connect with others
TIPS.caution: Giving should not leave you drained. Look after your own needs too.
TIPS.timeline: Some effects may be felt the same day; sustained improvements generally depend on weeks of repetition.

TIPS.title: Refer yourself to NHS Talking Therapies
TIPS.action: If you live in England and have anxiety or low mood, refer yourself online. You do not need to see a GP first.
TIPS.why: Talking therapies like CBT are free on the NHS and work well for anxiety and depression
TIPS.caution: This is not a crisis service. In a crisis, call 111 and choose the mental health option, or 999.
TIPS.timeline: Some effects may be felt the same day; sustained improvements generally depend on weeks of repetition.

TIPS.title: Call Tele MANAS on 14416
TIPS.action: For stress, low mood or any mental health worry, call Tele MANAS free on 14416 or 1-800-891-4416, day or night
TIPS.why: Trained counsellors answer in 20 languages, and can connect you to psychiatrists and in-person care
TIPS.caution: If someone is in immediate danger, call 112.
TIPS.timeline: Some effects may be felt the same day; sustained improvements generally depend on weeks of repetition.

TIPS.title: Call or text 988 when things feel too much
TIPS.action: Call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org, for free, confidential support at any hour
TIPS.why: You do not have to be suicidal to reach out; 988 helps with stress, loneliness, substance use and more
TIPS.caution: If someone is in immediate danger, call 911.
TIPS.timeline: Some effects may be felt the same day; sustained improvements generally depend on weeks of repetition.

TIPS.title: Set up one cleaner-air room
TIPS.action: Pick one room, close it off, and run a correctly sized air purifier there on smoky or high-AQI days
TIPS.why: One well-filtered room gives you a place to breathe cleaner air when the whole home cannot be filtered
TIPS.caution: Keep the room cool enough in hot weather. A purifier does not remove all gases.

notes.IN: Useful during winter smog in many north Indian cities.
